feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence: iteration 10 (mass 0.45 kg, five sensors at x = ±0.04 m, y = 0.06 m, 12 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.095 m) scored 556.7, the best so far, with oval finish 1.00 and s-bend finish 0.55. Iteration 5 (mass 0.6 kg, same row and track) scored 465.8, with s-bend finish 0.20, so reducing mass improved the s-bend. Sensing is not the limit: iteration 1 cut line loss by widening coverage but lost completions, and iteration 9 showed a 16 mm footprint is worse. In the controller I kept kp 3.5, kd 0.6, ki 0.2 and base_speed 1.4 unchanged, so the mass change is isolated. I have no measurement for this candidate. Read the next race as follows. If s-bend max_error falls below 0.05 m and the oval finish stays at 1.00, the lower mass is helping, and 0.40 kg is the design to keep. If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above about 0.43 or the oval finish drops, the minimum mass adds jitter, and 0.45 kg (iteration 10) is the final geometry.
requested_changes: If s-bend steering_oscillation stays under about 0.40 and the oval finish holds at 1.00, keep mass at 0.40 kg, since iteration 10 at 0.45 kg gave s-bend oscillation 0.36 and s-bend finish 0.55 with max_error 0.050 m.

If s-bend oscillation rises above about 0.43 or the oval finish falls below 1.00, return mass to 0.45 kg with the same five-sensor row. Evidence: iteration 10 (0.45 kg) is the best tested design at 556.7.

Keep wheel_track 0.095 m and the five-sensor row at x = ±0.04 m, y = 0.06 m, 12 mm footprints. Evidence: iteration 6 (x ±0.05 m) lowered the oval finish to 0.90, iteration 7 (y 0.07 m) pushed s-bend max_error to 0.0626 m, and iteration 9 (16 mm footprint) scored 373.0.
